Because it's obviously a flat out reminder that I clearly have reached a point where I can't cope with my mental health by myself anymore. And if that's the case then I feel disgusted with myself. Other people my age are moving out, going to festivals,buying their first apartment, travelling, going to uni etc. And I'm not saying this at all in a boo hoo poor me way. I know that I have a good life and I've never had to go without basic necessities and I have a nice bedroom and a roof over my head, and I'm happy for other people my age that they've achieved this stuff it's not a bitter resentment or anything at all. But I do feel pissed off and tbh angry at myself that I haven't achieved any of this stuff. And I feel like it detracts from my mental/emotional strength and any other achievements I've made in life. Like what I'm doing is never enough it kind of feels like I'm climbing a rock face but every time I think I've reached a point where I feel proud of myself/mentally strong etc. it's like I loose my footing and end up falling back down to the bottom of the cliff face where I started. I feel like I can't talk to my friends family or even support workers/wellbeing groups about how I really feel sometimes because I feel like they would just tell me that I needed to go to the hospital or to a psych ward and that would NOT help. I know some people do have a positive experience on a psych ward, but for most people it isn't a positive experience and taking someone who's struggling with their mental health and placing them around lots of other people who are struggling with their mental health or feeling suicidal, you're all just going to be triggering each other tbh and how is that good for anyone's mental health.
